$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for WIN-267 T3 (M4.1) — constructing the adapters at the
composition root, and making readiness report what was actually built. One
entry per refusal, carrying the file it lives in (repository-relative), the
EXACT text that implements it (`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), the
suites run, and the NAMED cases that were SEEN to go red (`kills`).
A SEPARATE FILE FROM mutations.json, which is WIN-260's shutdown ledger and
says so in its own purpose. Appending here would have made one file whose
entries only make sense read against two different dimensions.
`file` is REPOSITORY-relative, for the reason mutations-config.json gives:
this dimension's guards live in THREE homes — apps/core-api/src/,
package-relative path would resolve in one of them and not the others.
WHY AN ADAPTER PACKAGE IS IN A CORE-API LEDGER. Two of the entries below
UNREACHABLE until this dimension: with nothing constructing that adapter,
nobody had ever held a connection to a server that was down at boot. They
are this dimension's findings, so they are in this dimension's ledger, and
the cases that kill them are in apps/core-api because that is where the
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Replace an entry's `from` with its `to` in the
named file, run the suites it names, and confirm a NAMED case goes red — not
a module-load failure, which is VACUOUS and not a kill. Then revert and
vitest   pnpm --filter @platos/core-api exec vitest run src/composition/installation.test.ts
process  pnpm --filter @platos/core-api exec vitest run src/process.test.ts
THE `process` SUITE NEEDS `pnpm build:v1` FIRST. It spawns `node dist/main.js`
— the shipped artifact — so a mutation to a `src/` file is only in the binary
after a rebuild. A sweep that forgets this reports every process entry as
surviving, which is the vacuity this project has already paid for once.
NONE of these entries needs a database, a container or a network. Every store
in every case points at a host that does not resolve or a port nothing is
listening on, which is deliberate: readiness reports what was CONSTRUCTED,
and a process whose stores are down at boot must still start and say so.

mutations.name: T09 redis-cache: the unawaited readiness rejection is unhandled again, and the process dies
mutations.note: The first of the two defects wiring this adapter exposed. Nothing awaits `ready` until a command is issued, so a server unreachable AT CONSTRUCTION rejects it with no handler and Node kills the process — before any caller could turn the outage into MEMORY_CACHE_UNAVAILABLE, which is the whole design.

mutations.name: T10 redis-cache: close() stops disconnecting, so a refused connection keeps its retry timer
mutations.note: A `quit()` that could not be sent leaves the client in its reconnect loop with a live timer, so a process that has decided to stop keeps the event loop turning until the orchestrator forces it down. declaredUnfalsifiable.name: E01 the fault channel is unreachable from any valid platform configuration
measurement: `constructAdapters` has three error arms — a thrown
`AdapterConfigurationError` from the ORM client, a refused root key ring,
and a refused retry policy — and NOT ONE of them can be reached by any
environment `loadPlatformConfiguration` accepts. That is a property of the
configuration contract, not a gap in this dimension's testing, and it is
recorded here rather than claimed as three more kills.
MEASURED, ONE ARM AT A TIME.
keyring-envelope: `createRootKeyRing` refuses on a non-integer version,
a key that is not 64 hex characters, a version declared twice, an empty
ring, and an active version absent from the material.
`config/security.ts` pins PLATOS_SECURITY_ENCRYPTION_KEY to
`[0-9a-fA-F]{64}` and its required version to the integer range
1..1000000; `constructAdapters` keys the ring BY the active version, so
the ring is never empty, never doubled and always holds its active key.
Every refusal is unreachable.
model-router-providers: `createModelRouterProvidersAdapter` refuses only
an empty rule set, and the call passes `{}`, so it takes
DEFAULT_RETRY_POLICY. There is no configuration variable for a policy.
postgres-tenancy: `createTenancyDatabaseClient` throws on a URL the
client cannot parse and on a pool setting that is not a positive whole
number. The section anchor already refuses anything that is not an
absolute `postgres:`/`postgresql:` URL, and PLATOS_STORE_POSTGRES_POOL_MAX
and _STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS carry integer minima of 1.
SO THE ARMS ARE EXERCISED WHERE THEY CAN BE. `constructAdapters` takes the
ASSEMBLED sections rather than an environment, so
`installation.test.ts`'s "refuses a root key ring that will not parse"
hands it a `SecurityConfiguration` the loader would never produce, and T05
above is killed by that case. The keyring arm is therefore a real guard
with a real kill; what is unfalsifiable is the claim that an OPERATOR could
reach it, and that claim is not made.
THE ARMS ARE KEPT ANYWAY. Two of the three constructors return a `Result`
and one throws; handling an error arm by pushing a fault that stops the
process is strictly better than ignoring it, and the day a section's
validation is relaxed — or an adapter gains a refusal its section does not
anticipate — the arm is already there and already routed to EX_CONFIG.
